part.text: {"program": [{"kind": "config_ex", "dataflow": 1}, {"kind": "config_ld", "slot": 0, "stride_bytes": 32, "scale": 1.0}, {"kind": "config_ld", "slot": 1, "stride_bytes": 32, "scale": 1.0}, {"kind": "config_st", "stride_bytes": 128}, {"for": "j", "start": 0, "stop": {"expr": "N // 16"}, "step": 1, "body": [{"kind": "mvin", "slot": 1, "buf": "B", "offset": {"expr": "j*16"}, "spad_addr": 16, "cols": 16, "rows": 16}, {"kind": "mvin", "slot": 1, "buf": "B", "offset": {"expr": "512 + j*16"}, "spad_addr": 32, "cols": 16, "rows": 16}, {"for": "i", "start": 0, "stop": {"expr": "M // 16"}, "step": 1, "body": [{"kind": "mvin", "slot": 0, "buf": "A", "offset": {"expr": "i*512"}, "spad_addr": 0, "cols": 16, "rows": 16}, {"kind": "preload", "bd_spad_addr": 16, "out_addr": 2684354560}, {"kind": "compute", "accumulated": false, "a_spad_addr": 0, "bd_spad_addr": 4294967295}, {"kind": "mvin", "slot": 0, "buf": "A", "offset": {"expr": "i*512 + 16"}, "spad_addr": 0, "cols": 16, "rows": 16}, {"kind": "preload", "bd_spad_addr": 32, "out_addr": 3758096384}, {"kind": "compute", "accumulated": false, "a_spad_addr": 0, "bd_spad_addr": 4294967295}, {"kind": "mvout", "buf_offset": {"expr": "i*512 + j*16"}, "acc_addr": 2684354560, "cols": 16, "rows": 16}]}]}, {"kind": "fence"}], "rationale": "Loop over j (N/16=2) outer and i (M/16=3) inner so both B tiles for column block j stay resident in scratchpad rows 16-47 across all three m-tiles, loading each of the 4 B tiles exactly once (4 mvins). The single remaining scratchpad tile slot (row 0) forces 2 A-tile loads per output tile (12 A mvins), giving the minimum feasible DMA input of 16 tiles x 256 = 4096 bytes: holding 2 A tiles instead would leave only 1 B slot and force 12 B loads (4608 bytes), and 2A+2B residency (64 rows) exceeds the 48-row scratchpad. Each output tile does an overwrite compute for k=0 then an accumulate compute for k=1 (out_addr bit 30), followed immediately by mvout since the 16-row accumulator holds only one tile. K=32 gives 32*16384 <= 2147483647; all reductions are in increasing k order via sequential compute pairs. Total expanded commands: 51."}
